explanation: Fires on the token 'the'/'The' (including 'the' fused inside URLs like www.theatlantic.com). It peaks in boilerplate and formulaic contexts, mostly software license headers ('Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License")', 'published by the Free Software Foundation', 'The contents of this file') and lists of outlet names. Ordinary prose 'the' gets weak to moderate activation (5-30%).

Fires on word-internal or continuation subword tokens in the middle of long or technical words and identifiers (st-igm-atisation, sediment-ation, [3H], www.mm-ajunkie, Model-Compiler, version-number dots). The tokens share no meaning, so it reads as a generic mid-word / compound-continuation detector, and it is hard to predict which pieces fire strongly.

Very sparse. It fires strongly only on 'ip' in 'immunoprecipitation'. It gives weaker (20-35%) activation on related fragments: 'precipitation', 'RIP', 'Internet Protocol', 'prelim', 'cross-linked' and other subword pieces of scientific or chemical words. Roughly it tracks a 'pr(e)cip/IP/prelim' cluster of subwords plus scattered chemistry fragments.

Fires inside phrases that name an award, achievement or assessment criterion, on the head word or the linking preposition: 'Excellence in', 'Player of the Year', 'Best', 'most valuable player', 'measure of success', 'Success was defined', 'efficiency evaluation', 'possession of'. The strongest cases are award/honour and evaluation contexts. The 'possession of' (criminal charge) cases are a less clearly related offshoot.

Fires on a wide variety of unrelated tokens: an AngularJS directive key 'link', the '2'/'1' digit beginning a year after 'in', license names (MPL, afl-), ordinary nouns like 'view', 'home', 'stock', 'fields', 'personal'. No shared token identity or context is apparent.

Fires on an adjective or classifier word that modifies a following noun phrase, usually one meaning importance, prominence or category: 'important', 'major', 'popular', 'well known', 'top', 'critical', 'clinical', 'main', 'following', 'common'. It is strongest when the word sits in a plural/category frame such as 'a number of important processes', 'four major types' or 'the following ways'. Plain content nouns give weak activation.

Fires on 'to' in the stock patent opening 'The (present) invention/disclosure relates (generally) to ...' (about 80-100%). It also fires on nearby boilerplate in patent field-of-invention sentences ('a method of', 'tomography method'). Other patent-prose tokens get weak to moderate activation.

Fires on a heterogeneous set of tokens: code and markup positions (boost/preprocessor path, meta 'content=', the ' *' comment line before a license URL, '<' before an author email, 'filter'), plus ordinary prose words ('in series', 'wrong', 'Banking', 'national team'). No consistent token or context links them.

Fires on the subword or word 'cast'/'coast'/'cust'/'const' (Cast, CASTILLO, Coastal, coast, custards, constellations, const). It responds to the orthographic 'c?ast/cust/const' token family regardless of meaning (TV cast, coastline, casting a spell). Weaker activation for direction and region words like North/South and 'coastal'.

Fires on many unrelated tokens in mixed contexts: 'Elastic' in AWS Beanstalk, 'ear' in TearDown, LaTeX '\cup', CSS 'padding', verbs like 'fulfilling', 'raises', 'rings', 'opens', 'fill', 'create', and possessive 's. No common token or context is evident.

Fires on a token that ends a line and includes the newline, mainly in code: an opening bracket, paren or brace followed by a newline ('[
', '%{
', 'import (
', '(
'), or a comma/operator before a line break inside an unfinished expression. It is strongest when the line ends mid-structure so the construct continues on the next line. Sentence-ending '.
' or '.

' in prose gives only weak to moderate activation.

Fires on a heterogeneous mix: code tokens ('errors.New', '<script', 'require_once'), medical-term subword endings ('stenosis', 'tamponade', 'Rhythm', 'blood gas'), and section-header newlines ('About

', 'Club career

'). No single shared property.

Fires on anatomical location modifiers in biomedical text, on the word before an anatomical structure: laterality and position words ('left', 'right', 'dorsal', 'medial', 'lower', 'the' in 'on the outer surface') and adjectival anatomical suffixes ('popliteal', 'duodenal', 'mesenteric'). It is strongest when the token specifies which part of the body is meant (dorsal root, neural tube, left abducens nerve).

Fires on a subword or word that completes a multi-token proper name, acronym or fixed technical term: 'Alcatraz', 'receiver operating characteristic', 'cognitive-behavioral', 'OSHA', 'NMDA', 'LibVLC', 'Historic Places', 'Dead Sea', 'Phase III', 'echocardiography'. The context must already have started a well-known named entity or term so the token is predictable.

Fires on characters inside hexadecimal strings and hashes, such as git hashes, GUIDs, UUIDs, Unity guids, sha256 oids, object addresses and wikimedia hex paths. It is strongest for a hex fragment in the middle of a random-looking ID. Plain decimal numbers or code give weak or no activation.

Fires on miscellaneous tokens with no shared theme: 'IS' in 'AS IS', 'ov' in Sakharov, 'form', 'Q' in polyQ, 'was', 'E' in Vitamin E, '$' in a bcrypt hash, '-view', 'Banksy', 'copyright'. Activations are moderately high across very different contexts.

Fires mainly on subword pieces inside the names of mathematical or scientific eponyms and terms: 'Tetration', 'Fibonacci', 'Mandelbrot', 'zeta', 'Fanconi', 'Fibroblast', 'fetuin'. It is strongest for math terms ('Tetration', 'Fibonaccized'). Other rare subword fragments get weaker activation.

Fires on nouns for natural landscape and outdoor features, usually the head of a compound: 'river banks', 'sea level', 'panoramic views', 'ocean currents', 'mountain stream', 'clouds', 'sky', 'storm water', 'wind turbines', 'warm waters', 'pine trees'. Function words and unrelated nouns give weak activation.

Fires on the standalone space token, which appears before a number (or occasionally before a name or after punctuation) when the tokenizer splits off the space: 'seek[ ]25 years', 'Euthanizes[ ]4 Lions', 'in[ ]2016'. It is strongest in prose right before a quantity or digit. Hyphens and parens before numbers give weaker activation.

Fires on function words ('the', 'of', 'a', 'an', 'to', 'New') inside formulaic encyclopedic or legal phrases that lead to a named entity or category: 'Title 29 of the Code of Federal Regulations', 'in the genus', 'region of Vietnam', 'the U.S. state', 'is an autosomal', 'licensed under the Apache License'. The token is the connector before the predictable proper name or classification.

Fires on a later subword component inside a compound code identifier (snake_case or camelCase), on the piece after an underscore or case boundary: 'BOOST_BIND_VISIT_EACH', 'link_libraries', 'validateCSRF', 'resource_item_business', 'FT_BEGIN_HEADER', 'SetAwsConfig'. Ordinary prose gives no activation.
